newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Britain packs up helicopters in Hong Kong farewell.
newsitem.headline: Britain packs up helicopters in Hong Kong farewell.

text.p: Britain closed a chapter in its military history in Hong Kong on Tuesday when the garrison's six ageing Wessex helicopters flew their last sortie and were handed over in a sell-off to the Uruguayan air force.

The grey-and-green camouflaged helicopters made a sweeping ceremonial flypast across Hong Kong and barrelled along the highrise-lined corridor of Victoria Harbour in formation before returning to base at the international Kai Tak airport.

Struggling to be heard over the roar of commercial jets on the nearby runway, the leader of the No. 28 Army Cooperation Squadron told reporters the helicopters had served the Royal Air Force well and were far from obsolete.
"These aircraft have quite a lot of life left in them yet," Dick Barton said.
The 33-year-old helicopters have been used to patrol Hong Kong, track down illegal immigrants who jumped the Chinese border or sneaked in by sea, and for sea and mountain rescue operations.

They will make one final flight on Thursday to an area where they will have their rotors removed and gearboxes stripped before being loaded on a barge and taken to a nearby container terminal for shipment, Goodwin said.
"They'll be put on a ship and off they go to South America for a completely new life," he said. Uruguay plans to use the helicopters for search and rescue operations and firefighting.

The No. 28 Squadron, a tactical support unit that has been resident in Hong Kong since 1949, is one of the last units of the British forces to pull out ahead of the territory's handover to China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of British rule.
